title: [Chapitre] II. Réalisations topologiques des réseaux : notes manuscrites (06/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this 1986 chapter Grothendieck works with 'ficelles' (strings). A ficelle is a compact triangulated space X with two disjoint closed 'extremities' A and B. A 'lien' or 'ligne' C is a closed subset separating A from B. Cutting along C gives subdivided ficelles X_{A,C} and X_{B,C}. On p.10 he introduced equivalence classes and an order relation on ficelle structures; on p.12 he proves a transitivity lemma for successive cuts C, D, giving an induced linear (cyclic) order on lines.

This page restricts the class of allowed ficelles and lines by a topological property P.
- One may require A and B to be connected, contractible, or homeomorphic to a fixed space. The same applies to the lines.
- This defines a subclass, read as 'notons L_P'.
- For the earlier structural statements about the ordered set L (existence and equivalence of structures, order properties) to remain valid for L_P, the condition should not be imposed on A and B themselves. It should be imposed on S_A and S_B, the boundaries (links) of regular ('tubular') neighbourhoods of A and B in X. Here P is, for example, 'contractible' or 'homeomorphic to a fixed space'.
- The same restriction is placed on internal lines C: the boundaries of regular neighbourhoods of C in X_{A,C} and in X_{B,C} must have P.
- The point is that regular-neighbourhood boundaries are invariant under replacing A by a regular neighbourhood. This is exactly the operation used in the order and equivalence relation of p.10, so the restricted class is stable.

Examples:
1) P = 'reduced to a point'. Each end and each line is joined to the rest at a single point, so locally the ficelle looks like an arc. One obtains, in his words, 'la théorie des diagrammes top. ord.', presumably 1-dimensional ordered topological diagrams.
2) (next page) P = 'homeomorphic to a ball B^n'. One gets decompositions of a band I×B^n ≅ B^{n+1}, with ends {0}×B^n and {1}×B^n, by 'lines' homeomorphic to B^n. For n=1 these are pictures of pseudoline-like cuts of a strip.

Purpose: to build topological realizations of combinatorial 'réseaux' (networks / arrangements) by strings cut by lines, with control on local topology.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is programmatic. The claim that imposing P on regular-neighbourhood boundaries preserves the previous properties of L is asserted, not proved. Since p.10 already records that some earlier claims were false ('Faux déjà ... dans le cas des segments'), the earlier properties themselves are partly in doubt.

ideas.what: Restricting ficelles and lines to a class L_P defined by a topological property P imposed on the boundaries of regular neighbourhoods of the ends and of the internal lines, rather than on the subsets themselves.
ideas.modern_name: Conditions on links / regular neighbourhood boundaries (PL topology); 'locally flat'- or 'collared'-type conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Regular neighbourhood theory: J.H.C. Whitehead (1939), Rourke–Sanderson

ideas.what: Example P = point: recovering a theory of ordered topological (1-dimensional) diagrams.
Example P = ball: decompositions of I×B^n by separating n-balls (continued on the next page).
ideas.modern_name: Pseudohyperplane / pseudoline-type slicings of a ball; related to the topological representation of oriented matroids

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'ficelles' with lines whose regular-neighbourhood boundaries are balls give a framework close to topological representations of arrangements (pseudolines, pseudohyperplanes, oriented matroids). The linear order on lines derived on p.12 resembles wiring diagrams. This link to the oriented-matroid literature is not made in the literature on Grothendieck's 1980s work.
missed.quote: les bords des voisin. tub. des C dans X_{A,C} et X_{B,C} ont la propriété P
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may offer an intrinsic, PL-topological axiomatization of 'topological realizations of networks', comparable to the Folkman–Lawrence representation theorem. It remains only sketched here.

missed.claim: The programme is stated but not carried out: classify or characterize ficelle structures in L_P for general P (connected, contractible, given homeomorphism type) and check that the order and equivalence properties survive.
missed.quote: Pour que les conditions plus haut sur l'ens. ordonné L soient aussi vraies pour L_P, il est bon d'exiger ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. This is a natural but limited research thread within his own framework.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a definitional, programmatic page. Imposing conditions on regular-neighbourhood boundaries is standard PL practice. The only mildly interesting aspect is the unpublished framework itself and its implicit proximity to pseudoline and oriented-matroid realizations.
transcription_corrections: 'pour l'ensemble[?] admissible[?] $\mathcal{L}$' is likely 'sur l'ens. ordonné $\mathcal{L}$' ('ordonné' is underlined); 'soient aussi vraies' is then readable.
Line 5 is likely 'd'espace P propriété intrinsèque/topologique', with the correction inserted above 'notons'.
Line 3: 'voire ≃' — the symbol is probably '≃' (homotopy-equivalent) or a struck-out mark before 'homéomorphes à un espace donné'.
'[-correspondante,-]' appears to be 'correspondante' with a curved stroke, possibly not deleted.
